name: Jindal Steel Ltd.
business_summary: Odisha/Chhattisgarh-based integrated steel maker (Raigarh, Angul) with crude capacity just lifted to 15.6 Mtpa after the second Angul blast furnace; FY27 production guided ~11 Mt (6 Mt in H2) and sales 10.5-11 Mt. Mix ~60:40 flats:longs (target 65:35): plates (>220 kt/month for defence, shipbuilding, wind), HRC, rails, structurals, TMT; value-added share 57%. Captive iron ore (Kasia), 15 Mtpa captive coal blocks, coal-gasification-based DRI, and overseas coal mines (Mozambique). Q2 FY27 consolidated: sales Rs16,610 cr (+45%), EBITDA Rs2,504 cr (15.1%), adj. EBITDA/t Rs10,522, PAT Rs774 cr; net debt Rs14,790 cr (1.51x). Mcap Rs1.18 lakh cr.

revenue_mix.segment: traded goods, power, mining and other

exposures.mechanism: Integrated flat+long producer; ~95% of revenue is steel at NSR Rs70,078/t (Q2 FY27). +7% (SSU) = ~Rs4,900/t x FY27E sales 10.6 Mt (MOFSL) = ~Rs5,200 cr vs FY27E consolidated EBITDA Rs12,830 cr => +40% EBITDA. EV/MCap 1.13 (mcap Rs1,17,698 cr + net debt Rs14,790 cr); persistence 0.4 (prices already ~Rs60,000/t, H2 contracts reset; Chinese/safeguard cap) => 40 x 1.13 x 0.4 = +18; trimmed to +16 for partial pricing-in (HRC +14% from Q2 average by Oct). Consistent with spec worked example. Empirical pack has no significant steel factor (F_STEEL_GLOBAL not in top 12), stock beta 1.3 dominates.

evidence.note: NSR INR70,078/t Q2; TMT 52k->59-60k/t, HRC 51-53k->~60k/t; mgmt expects better H2 realisations
FY27E EBITDA Rs128.3bn, sales 10.6 Mt; steel price rally
Indian HRC at four-year high

exposures.mechanism: GROSS direct cost effect (pass-through to prices travels separately via F_COKING_COAL->F_STEEL_INDIA 0.3 in backbone, so net is much smaller: -7.5 + 0.3x16 = -2.7). Imported coking coal ~0.55 t/t steel (model estimate; captive thermal coal + coal-gas DRI lowers BF coke intensity) at ~US$250/t (unverified) x USD/INR 94.5 = ~Rs13,000/t steel = ~22% of costs (NSR 70,078 minus EBITDA 10,800 = Rs59,300/t). +15% = US$37/t = Rs3,500/t coal => Rs1,950/t steel = -18% EBITDA/t; x1.13 x persistence 0.4 => -8.2; trimmed to -7.5 for Mozambique/captive supply. Mgmt: coking coal +US$12-15/t in Q2 (EBITDA/t fell 12% QoQ to Rs10,522) and a further +US$20-25/t in Q3; may ease Dec-Jan if Russian Black Sea supply resumes.

evidence.note: Coking coal +US$12-15/t Q2, further +US$20-25/t Q3; Mozambique mine ships ~2 vessels/month
Russian Black Sea coal could ease prices Dec-Jan
Coking coal +25% in Aug 2026

exposures.mechanism: Ore/pellet ~12% of costs (~Rs7,100/t steel, model estimate). Captive Kasia mine = 33% of consumption (Q2), OMC long-term 13.5 Mt agreement, NMDC; ~65% market-linked. +15% x 12% x 0.65 = +1.2% of costs = Rs725 cr = -5.7% EBITDA; x1.13 x 0.4 = -2.6. Iron ore is FALLING (-12.5% since 1 Jun, two-year low), so this is currently a tailwind; empirical elasticity is +1.53 (t=+1.0) - wrong sign but insignificant (iron ore co-moves with China steel demand sentiment), hence upper bound set positive.

evidence.note: Kasia 33% of iron ore consumption in Q2; OMC LTA 13.5 Mt; supplies normalised
Iron ore at two-year low (US$91.95/t on 2026-11-05)

exposures.mechanism: Domestic thermal coal feeds coal-gas DRI (Angul, Raigarh), captive power and syngas. Captive mines (~15 Mtpa Raigarh+Angul, incl. Gare Palma) cover 50-55% of need (target 65-70%); rest via linkage/e-auction where premiums reached ~94% in Sep-Oct 2026. Coal+gas ~10% of costs (Rs6,200 cr), ~47% bought = Rs2,900 cr; +10% = Rs290 cr = -2.3% EBITDA x1.13 x0.5 = -1.3. Utkal B2 mine (FY27) and 50% royalty exemption on coal-gasification coal improve this.

evidence.note: Captive coal 50-55% of needs, target 65-70%; Utkal B2 within FY27; 50% royalty exemption
74 thermal plants <=7 days stock; e-auction premium ~94% (domain-b 12 Oct)

exposures.mechanism: User worked-example channel (electricity). BF-BOF + DRI route uses ~450 kWh/t = ~5 BU/yr at 11 Mt; most from captive plants (coal-fired, waste-heat, BF gas), assume ~30% bought/open-access at ~Rs6/unit = Rs900 cr (1.5% of costs). +15% (SSU) = Rs135 cr = -1.1% EBITDA x1.13 x0.4 = -0.5. IEX day-ahead hit the Rs20/unit ceiling on 19 Sep 2026 and Q2 prices were ~+46% y/y, so realised exposure could be larger than the SSU; MOFSL names 'power & fuel' among Q2 cost escalators. Share of bought power is NOT disclosed - low confidence. Indirect power-crunch channels (rail rake priority, grid curtailment) are in the md narrative.

evidence.note: Q2 costs escalated on raw material, power & fuel and freight
IEX hits Rs20/kWh ceiling; Q2 spot ~+46% y/y
Coal-crunch blackouts hit Indian factories; captive producers disadvantaged (search snippet)

exposures.mechanism: Mixed. +3% INR depreciation: (i) coking coal import cost +3% on ~22% of costs = +0.7% of costs = -3.4% EBITDA; (ii) domestic steel prices anchored to import parity so ~40% passes to NSR = +1.2% of NSR = +8% EBITDA; (iii) exports ~8% of volume (HRC/plates, ~100 kt/month) +3% = +1.6% EBITDA; (iv) USD debt/ECB and overseas subsidiaries (Oman, Mozambique, Australia) small net negative. Net ~+6% EBITDA x1.13 x0.3 = +2; shaded to +1 since import-parity pass-through is imperfect under safeguard. No significant empirical estimate (F_USDINR absent from top-12).

evidence.note: Exports ~0.1 Mt/month; adj. EBITDA includes INR0.68bn forex gain
Pack: USD/INR not among significant factors

exposures.mechanism: Gross debt ~Rs18,000-22,000 cr (PL: FY27E Rs180bn), net debt Rs14,790 cr (1.51x EBITDA); ~50% floating. +25 bp x ~Rs10,000 cr = Rs25 cr = 0.2% of EBITDA => ~-0.2; RBI hiked to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026 (calibrated tightening) so more hikes are live (Dec 4 MPC). Demand channel (housing -> TMT) is carried by F_HOUSING_DEMAND and backbone edges.

evidence.note: Net debt INR147.9bn, ND/EBITDA 1.51x; capex INR75-100bn FY27 from internal accruals
RBI hikes repo 25 bp to 5.50%

exposures.mechanism: Capital-intensive cyclical with a ramp-up story (EV/EBITDA 6.3x FY28E, P/E 11.5x FY28E but 20x FY27E per PL): +25 bp on cost of equity with effective duration ~8-10 on the FY28-29 earnings step-up => ~-1.5 to -2%. 10y G-sec ~7.4-7.45% after RBI liquidity drain. Not separable from market beta (1.3) in the data.

evidence.note: Market beta 1.3-1.4; P/E 34.5 TTM
EV/EBITDA 9.1x FY27E, 6.3x FY28E

exposures.mechanism: User worked-example channel (China dumping). PRICE effect is already carried by backbone F_CHINA_STEEL_EXPORTS->F_STEEL_GLOBAL (-0.35)->F_STEEL_INDIA (0.525)->JINDALSTEL(+16) = -2.9 per +15% y/y; this direct edge covers only the VOLUME/EXPORT-MARKET effect: lost export volumes (~8% of sales into Europe/Asia) and import share gain that the 12% safeguard (to 11.5% Apr 2027) only partly blocks (H1 FY27 imports +24%). China Sep exports 10.49 Mt (+3.3% m/m); Europe's turn to protection (EU quota/CBAM) diverts Chinese tonnes to Asia.

evidence.note: China September steel exports 10.492 Mt
H1 FY27 steel imports +24%, demand outpaces output
India steel exports to EU -20% in H1 FY27

exposures.mechanism: DGTR opened an AD probe on hot-rolled flat steel from China, Japan and Russia on 26 Jun 2026 (final ~Jun 2027, provisional possible earlier). Flats are ~60-65% of JSP's mix (plates 220 kt/month, HRC). Incremental effective protection over the existing 12% safeguard assumed ~+4-5 pp => HRC +2% = 0.3 SSU x16 = +4.8, probability-neutral conditional weight shaded to +3. Counter-signal: steel ministry reportedly unlikely to seek new curbs (Reuters 6 Oct).

evidence.note: DGTR AD probe on HR flat steel from China, Japan, Russia
Safeguard duty expected to keep domestic prices steady

exposures.mechanism: Plates, rails, structurals and HRC go to infrastructure, defence, shipbuilding, windmills (plates >220 kt/month). +10% government capex growth ~ +1.3% Indian steel demand; JSP is capacity-led so volume effect is small and the price effect is already in the steel-price edge; kept low to avoid double count (flag parallel path via backbone F_GOVT_CAPEX->F_STEEL_INDIA). Union Budget 1 Feb 2027 is the catalyst.

evidence.note: Defence, merchant vessel, shipbuilding and windmill demand supportive; construction to improve H2
Plate output >220 kt/month

exposures.mechanism: Long products (rebar/TMT, ~35-40% of mix, shifting to 35%) depend on housing/construction; TMT output cut to 120 kt/month from 220 kt and redirected to flats, which cuts sensitivity. +10% sales volume ~ +1.5% long-product demand; weight small after mix shift. Rate-hike channel: RBI repo 5.50% -> mortgage rates -> housing (backbone F_REPO_IN->F_HOUSING_DEMAND -0.27).

evidence.note: TMT production reduced to 120 kt/month from 220 kt; targeting 65:35 flats:longs

exposures.mechanism: Ocean freight on imported coking coal (US/Australia/Mozambique) ~9% of CFR cost; +25% freight = +2% of coking-coal cost (~Rs260/t steel) = -2.4% EBITDA/t x1.13 x0.3 = -0.8. PL cites higher ocean freight in Q2 costs; Red Sea/Hormuz disruption keeps rates elevated.

evidence.note: Adj. EBITDA/t Rs10,522 despite higher raw material and ocean freight costs

exposures.mechanism: Cost inflation from West Asia only ~US$4-5/t because JSP replaced imported propane (~Rs100/kg) and natural gas with coal-gas syngas (~Rs30/kg) in reheating/galvanising; peers on LPG/propane are worse off (relative positive). Escalation still lifts diesel/freight/coking-coal logistics and risk-off (market beta 1.3), net -0.8. Positive wedge: higher demand for domestic plates/defence.

evidence.note: West Asia cost inflation limited to ~USD4-5/t via coal gasification
Timely switch to methane from coal gasification avoided productivity loss in LPG crisis

exposures.mechanism: Captive iron ore (Kasia), coal (Gare Palma, Utkal B2) and OMC/NMDC ore pricing all embed royalty/DMF/auction premia; +1 (assume +2 pp of royalty) on ~Rs3,000 cr captive output value = Rs60 cr = -0.5% EBITDA, structural persistence 1.0 x1.13 => -0.6; widened for auction-premium risk on new coal/ore blocks. Positive side: stated 50% royalty exemption on coal for gasification.

evidence.note: Expects government incentives incl. stated 50% royalty exemption on eligible gasification coal

exposures.mechanism: Empirical -0.89 per +5 VIX points (t=-2.0, market beta 1.32): high-beta cyclical sold in risk-off; shrunk slightly toward 0 since part is already the market beta that the Director demeans. Also correlated with US equities (+1.60, t=2.1) and aluminium/copper (+2.4/+1.9, t=2.7/2.5) - these are China/global-cyclical proxies, not fundamental links (JSP has no Al/Cu business).
